title: China’s ‘Internet Addiction’ Schools Are Now Locking Up Adults
gist: China's private disciplinary institutions have extended from minors to legal adults: a 21-year-old Beijing music student was seized by relatives and institution employees posing as police, driven to Henan province, and confined for 11 days at a facility charging 26,800 yuan (about $4,000) for six months.

insights.claim: A 21-year-old music student in Beijing was forcibly taken in March by her father, aunt, and two employees of a private disciplinary institution who were falsely presented to her as police officers investigating a family matter.
insights.speaker: Lina Ma
insights.so_what: Impersonating police to abduct a legal adult signals these institutions operate with effectively no enforcement risk — a regulatory gap that could close abruptly.
insights.quote: Her relatives told her the strangers were police officers investigating a family matter.

insights.claim: The student's phone was confiscated and she was driven hundreds of miles to an institution in Henan province where she was held for 11 days, showing these facilities operate across provincial lines to place detainees far from local support.
insights.speaker: Lina Ma
insights.so_what: Cross-province operation complicates jurisdiction and enforcement, which is precisely why the sector persists despite periodic crackdowns.
